productLossClosed: Rapid thread-mode changes no longer dispatch concurrently. Renderer and main serialize runtime and interaction-mode commands per thread while preserving concurrency across different threads.
An older failed command cannot delete or roll back a newer pending Plan or Build intent.
A newer failed command returns to the most recent successful intent instead of an obsolete pre-mutation snapshot.

Main consumes the orchestration DispatchResult sequence and retains accepted pending state until the authoritative shell snapshot has reached that command, preventing ABA reconciliation against a stale repeated mode value.
Renderer keeps canonical mode snapshots separate from optimistic projection and only reconciles accepted mutations against canonical shell state.
remainingEvidenceDebt: Exact Native physical default-to-Plan-to-default tapping remains pending-user-session. The DevTool mutation path previously lost its localhost:8903 response channel and is not counted as interaction proof.
The retained exact Native runs prove current persisted Plan state, production bundle health, material, geometry, main transport, and cleanup. They do not lower the existing interaction residual.

A dedicated delay/failure injection through a live packaged renderer would improve integration coverage but is not required to prove the pure ordering state machine or the authoritative sequence gate.
harnessMismatch: Earlier DevTool touch and typed connector mutation attempts returned No response found for clientId: localhost:8903 while the session was active. Those runs remain excluded from product attribution.
No browser or Native screenshot is used to claim rapid-toggle interaction behavior; the race proof is deterministic source-level ordering and receipt-sequence coverage.
classification.evidenceBoundary: This evidence records a repaired P1 race and clean post-fix runtime health without changing the fixed denominator or any fidelity residual. Physical Native input remains uncredited.
